title: Jump not edge-triggered: hold-space repeat + sidewall double-jump
description: Holding space lets you jump higher/repeatedly and lets you 'double jump' off a block beside you. Confirmed in src/player.c:242-245 — jump condition checks the polled boolean in->space (frame snapshot applied to every physics tick this frame, player.c:309-331), NOT an edge transition, so any tick where on_ground is true while space is held fires a jump. Grounded detection (physics.c:93-106 aabb_supported) only checks the slot directly below, but corner/micro-collisions while sliding down a wall can set on_ground for a tick or two, allowing a jump against a sidewall. Fix: edge-trigger jump (jump only on space press transition), optionally add small coyote-time; ensure grounded detection ignores transient sidewall contacts. Add pure-function test.

title: Player falls through terrain and dies (tunneling / no spawn-safety)
description: Players sometimes pass through solid terrain, end up underground, and die (fall damage / void). Confirmed causes in src/physics.c: (1) substep threshold (physics.c:71-88) only splits when a single-axis delta >0.999, insufficient near terminal velocity (~1.3 blocks/tick) so high-speed motion can tunnel; (2) axis-order sequential collision resolution (physics.c:21-69, applied Y->X->Z) can recompute bounds (lines 65-67) into a new overlap and embed the player; (3) no spawn-safety check that the player isn't embedded in blocks (main.c spawn_y = worldgen height + 4 assumes safe). Fix: swept/continuous collision or per-tick substepping by velocity magnitude; embed-resolution that pushes OUT to nearest free space; spawn-safety validation. Add pure-function collision tests (see tests/test_block_physics.c).

title: GPU-aware default graphics preset (discrete vs integrated)
description:
Root-cause fix for the quality regression introduced in 57c4d96 'feat(perf): add low-end GPU settings'. That commit turned the previously-hardcoded 4x MSAA / 16x aniso into tunable settings but defaulted them to the integrated-GPU-safe low end (msaa=1, aniso=4, render_distance=12) for EVERYONE. Result: discrete-GPU desktops now render aliased edges + a near fog wall by default, looking worse than the pre-57c4d96 build with no actual perf benefit on capable hardware.

pick_physical_device() in renderer.c:189 already classifies the chosen GPU as DISCRETE vs INTEGRATED. Use that to choose the startup preset: discrete -> High, integrated -> Medium/Low. CLI flags and (later) the saved settings file still override.

Subtlety: render_settings_default() runs at arg-parse time, BEFORE the device is picked, so the default must be resolved after pick_physical_device (or re-resolved once the GPU type is known, only for fields the user did not explicitly override via CLI).
design: Depends on the preset table. Track which fields were explicitly set on the CLI so GPU-aware defaults only fill the untouched ones. This issue is shippable independently of the settings UI and is the quickest user-visible win.
acceptance_criteria: On a discrete GPU with no CLI graphics flags, startup logs a High-ish preset (msaa>=4, render_distance>=16); on integrated, the conservative preset; explicit CLI flags always win. Selection logic is a pure, unit-tested function.

title: Biome border blending
description: Smooth height transitions between adjacent biomes to remove visible cliffs/walls. Root cause confirmed: biome_classify() uses hard noise thresholds (biome.c:66, elevation>0.35 => mountains) so adjacent columns can flip biome abruptly, then worldgen adds a DISCRETE additive height bias per biome (worldgen.c:163-178; biome_height_bias biome.c:153-163, mountains +24, desert -2). The +24 vs +0 step materializes as an instant cliff at the border. Fix: interpolate/blend the height bias (and ideally terrain params) across a transition band using a smoothed biome weight per column instead of a hard switch. Pure + tested (biome.c is already pure).

comments.author: Samu Toljamo
comments.text: Partially done (branch worktree-agent-a9532786fedb7e8bd, commit 8364bdf). DONE: net_resolve() via getaddrinfo replaces inet_pton in main.c — --client now accepts DNS hostnames and IPv4 literals (resolves A records; AAAA-only results reported distinctly via NET_RESOLVE_NO_IPV4). Pure + unit-tested (test_resolve_addr). REMAINING: full IPv6 transport. title: EPIC: server-authoritative chunk streaming (stop client-side regen)

Gold-standard fix: server owns chunks and STREAMS chunk data (and edits) to clients; clients stop regenerating. Needs a chunk-transfer protocol (use the reliable fragmentation already added), compression, and client-side chunk receive/apply. Large. Interim mitigation tracked separately (on-demand server gen + overlay-on-join).

title: Graphics quality presets (Low/Medium/High/Ultra + Custom)

Rough preset table (tune later):
- Low:    render_distance 8,  msaa 1, aniso 1,  render_scale 0.75, present FIFO
- Medium: render_distance 12, msaa 1, aniso 4,  render_scale 1.0,  present FIFO

- Ultra:  render_distance 24, msaa 4, aniso 16, render_scale 1.0,  present MAILBOX

Requested values are still clamped to device caps at apply time (msaa/aniso already clamp).
design: Pure data: a static preset table + preset_to_settings(preset) and a settings_match_preset(settings) helper (returns preset or CUSTOM). Keep in a small pure module with a unit test (project TDD convention). UI (dyb.3.3) and GPU-aware defaults consume this.

title: Runtime-mutable RenderSettings (apply graphics changes without restart)
description:
Today RenderSettings is read once at startup (render_settings_default() in renderer.h, overridden by CLI flags in main.c) and baked into the renderer at init: MSAA sample count is picked once, the sampler aniso is fixed at sampler-create, render_scale sizes the offscreen target once, render_distance is passed to world_create once. A settings UI is useless unless these can change at runtime.

Plumb runtime re-application for each field:
- msaa -> rebuild MSAA color target + render pass + graphics pipelines (pick_sample_count path in renderer.c).
- render_scale -> recreate offscreen render target + blit at new size.
- aniso -> recreate the block-atlas sampler (texture.c:286 region).
- present -> swapchain rebuild (the existing swapchain-recreate path likely covers this).
- render_distance -> adjust world streaming radius live (world.c) without a full reload if feasible; otherwise re-stream.

This is the foundational enabler for dyb.3.3 (UI) and the preset/GPU-default work.
design: Prefer a single renderer_apply_settings(Renderer*, RenderSettings old, RenderSettings new) that diffs fields and rebuilds only what changed, reusing existing swapchain/pipeline recreate code paths. Must be safe to call between frames (idle the device like swapchain recreate does).
acceptance_criteria: Changing each of msaa/render_scale/aniso/present/render_distance at runtime takes visible effect with no crash/validation errors; unit-testable diff logic (which subsystems need rebuild for a given old->new) factored as a pure function with a tests/test_*.c target.

notes: ARCHITECTURE (investigated): mobs render from ONE shared GPU-baked humanoid mesh (player_model.c bakes a single PlayerModel; renderer.c holds one; renderer_frame.c draws all mob+player states with it). Per-type variation today = two-tone color + per-axis scale only (mob_render.c MobRenderDef + shaders/player.frag). True per-type meshes require: per-type vertex/index buffers in renderer.c/h, mesh selection in renderer_frame.c, mob-type passed via render state in main.c. So 0xm = the RENDERER-WIRING step; it needs main.c (owned by combat agent) + renderer*. Do AFTER combat-feedback wave frees main.c. Consumes the pure box-model data from the groundwork ticket.
